thread:
maya: Short design question: do we do canary bucket assignment at the edge (LB) or centrally? Need session affinity for cache warmup and an automatic fallback if quality/latency regresses. Pros/cons?

omar: Central controller: single source of truth for rollout state + easy to flip back. Con: control-plane outage could slow requests or require edge fallbacks.

liz: Important to distinguish user-session affinity vs. host affinity. For cache warmup we want host affinity (same worker host) not just route affinity. That increases stickiness requirements.

kevin: Edge decision avoids per-request control-plane RPCs and reduces reaction latency. But we then have to distribute rollout logic + signal TTLs to every edge binary. More rollout surface to test.

maya: Our biggest worry is cold-cache p99 when we flip traffic. Shadow warmup helps but only if the same client keeps hitting warmed hosts.

dena: What about a hybrid: control-plane publishes a short-lived signed "rollout token" per region. Edges verify signature and read rollout buckets locally. Control-plane rotates token on policy change. Gives central policy + edge autonomy.

omar: Love that. Token should include: rollout_id, expiry_ts, buckets spec, sticky_window_seconds, fallback_policy shorthand, signature. Edge only verifies sig, reads buckets, does hash/assign.

kevin: Pseudo example token payload (illustrative only):
```
rollout_id: r-2026-03-21-7
expiry_ts: 1754325600
buckets: [{"variant":"canary","pct":10},{"variant":"stable","pct":90}]
sticky_window: 3600
fallback_policy: "same-region->cross-region->lower-tier"
sig: "base64.."
```
Edge verifies sig and uses the bucket table. If token expired, edge falls back to baseline route.

liz: Observability: token must carry rollout_id so traces and logs can correlate. Edges should tag traces with rollout_id and variant assignment + warmed_cache=true/false probe flag.

emily: From SRE POV, fallback precedence needs to be explicit in token or tenant config. Ops may want region-first for latency-sensitive tenants, or variant-first for cost-sensitive ones. Make it configurable.

dena: For token rotation: publish via region-local pub/sub for near-immediate delivery; fallback to TTL expiry so stale tokens self-expire. Invalidation should be best-effort but fast.

omar: Also include a revision_number and absolute expiry. Absolute expiry + revision avoids ambiguity when clocks drift or messages reorder.

maya: How do we ensure rollback propagation isn't a blind spot? If control-plane says rollback, but pub/sub drops, expiry covers us but could be slow. Do we add an aggressive short-circuit kill switch?

emily: Manual kill switch should rotate token to a baseline-only token with near-immediate invalidation push. Runbook: rotate token -> publish invalidation -> check region subscribers -> if >30s elapsed, escalate.

kevin: Warmup cost: full duplication capacity for warm hosts is expensive. Alternative pattern: shadow traffic to warm hosts (they accept requests but mark responses as shadowed) and use sticky session mapping so real traffic later lands on warmed host. Need to model extra network/compute cost.

liz: Probe schema suggestion: minimal probe event from edge -> control plane: { rollout_id, variant, probe_latency_ms, warmed_cache:true|false, error_count, sample_id }. Keep it small and high-cardinality safe.

omar: For gating the canary, control-plane computes a canary_health score from aggregated probes: weighted error_rate, p99 latency, warmed_cache_ratio, quality_metrics if available. If canary_health < threshold -> rotate token to force baseline.

dena: Security: use short-lived signing keys rotated by control-plane KMS. Edge should fetch public key bundle periodically. Token sig verification must be constant-time and fail-safe -> reject unknown keys.

maya: Action items from this thread:
- prototype rollout-token on edge (omar + dena)
- draft probe schema + trace tags (liz + emily)
- cost sim for shadow warmup vs. reserved warm hosts (kevin + maya)
- ops runbook for immediate rollback + invalidation SLA (emily)

deploy-bot: Queued: rollout-token-proto -> staging (#1288). ETA ~10m.

omar: I'll open the token format PR today. Question: include full fallback rule grammar in token vs shorthand? I prefer a compact fallback_policy id in token and resolver at edge for small tokens.

liz: Agree shorthand + resolver. Keep token size small to avoid blowup in headers.

emily: Also log rollout_id in biz metrics so paging/alerting can map regressions to active rollouts.

maya: Thanks everyone. I'll write a short RFC summarizing hybrid token-based approach + probe gating and tag owners. Will include simulation hypotheses for warmup cost. :slightly_smiling_face:
